title: p256-ecdlp: odd-lift BSGS with global LSD distribution and implicit sixteen-ary lookup

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P on NIST P-256 with the profile generator P, the deterministic odd-lift baby-step/giant-step procedure in proof.md recovers x with probability 1. Baby records are ordered by a global LSD byte distribution with one histogram per byte and no heap. Giants are located by an implicit sixteen-ary descent on that array. Total classical work is strictly less than 2^(1329/10) target-group-operation equivalents at C=1000, including preprocessing, sorting, lookup, verification and failed-path charging. Peak memory is strictly less than 2^135 bytes. Preprocessing is strictly less than 2^132 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in the total. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. No heuristic premise, quantum step or uncharged table is used.

experiments.purpose: Exhaustively recover every scalar on a prime-order toy curve with the odd-lift decomposition, check that global LSD sorting is a stable permutation with cross-page scatters, and check that implicit sixteen-ary lookup hits the sorted key. This does not measure production instruction counts or memory.
